messages:
maria (People Ops): Jordan asked whether they can take a 401(k) loan now and simultaneously roll an old-plan balance into Redwood while going on unpaid leave next month. Wants to avoid repayment gaps or taxable distribution. Any quick guidance?

helen (Benefits): Short: loans are plan-specific. You can take a loan from the current plan and we generally accept incoming rollovers, but outstanding loans rarely transfer as a loan to a new plan. If you roll funds in, the old loan often must be settled first or left with the old provider.

sam (Payroll): From payroll side: loan repayments happen via a deduction code on each pay. If you're going on unpaid leave, payroll won't collect repayments for unpaid periods. That can trigger a defaulted loan scenario if the vendor treats missed repayments as default. We need to coordinate timing carefully.

jordan (IC): So if I get the loan now and then go on 8 weeks unpaid, will vendor automatically pause repayments or classify as default? I don't want surprises.

helen (Benefits): Vendors vary. Some allow temporarily suspending repayments for approved unpaid leave; others do not and may treat missed payments as a deemed distribution (taxable). We can request a repayment-suspension with the vendor but it usually requires documentation (leave dates) and vendor approval.

maria (People Ops): Action: Helen to check vendor policy on leave suspension for loans; Sam to confirm payroll behavior for short-term leaves and mapping for loan deduction codes. Jordan to decide whether to delay loan until after leave or take now with documented suspension.

sam (Payroll): Practical note: if vendor requires loan to be repaid during leave and there are no payroll deductions, vendor may offset the outstanding balance by issuing a taxable distribution. If that happens, payroll needs to reflect it for W-2/1099 reporting. Better to get vendor confirmation before taking loan.

helen (Benefits): Also note rolling funds in doesn't change loan rules. If you roll pre-tax amounts into our plan, the loan status doesn't magically transfer. If you want to consolidate, options: 1) repay loan before rollover, 2) leave loan with old plan (if allowed), 3) request distribution for outstanding loan (taxable) then rollover remaining. We'll document options.

jordan (IC): If I delay loan until after leave, can I still roll in old-plan funds now so I have account consolidated? Or does rollover timing affect loan eligibility?

helen (Benefits): You can do a direct rollover anytime; it won't affect your ability to take a new loan from Redwood after rollover, provided plan rules (service and contribution history) allow a loan immediately. Some plans require a waiting period; I'll confirm ours.

maria (People Ops): Legal check: @legal-bot do we need special language for leaves + loan suspensions to avoid de facto discrimination?

legal-bot: Quick note: treat all participants consistently. If loan-suspension for leave is allowed, document the objective criteria and obtain vendor confirmation in writing. Avoid ad-hoc exceptions.

sam (Payroll): Ticket LOAN-2026-411 opened: "verify vendor loan suspension policy + payroll mapping for loan deductions during unpaid leave". ETA 3 business days.

helen (Benefits): I'll ask vendor for their leave suspension form/e-sign and confirm whether they allow resume-on-date. Also will check if outstanding loan necessitates any participant authorization to avoid default.

jordan (IC): Thanks. If vendor offers suspension e-sign, can I sign now and still take the loan before leave? Or does suspension only apply after loan is active?

helen (Benefits): Good Q. Usually suspension applies once a loan is active; some vendors allow you to set an expected leave start so suspension starts on that date. We'll ask them to confirm. If not, safest route is take loan and immediately request suspension with leave docs.

maria (People Ops): Plan: Helen to post vendor response in this thread. Sam to note any payroll changes needed (manual deduction on return). Jordan to decide but lean toward waiting if vendor can't guarantee suspension. We'll update handbook FAQ after closure.

jordan (IC): Appreciate it. Please flag if taking loan now risks a taxable distribution during leave. I'll wait for vendor confirm before signing anything. :thumbsup:
